plain: Following as a result or logical outcome.

webster.text: Following, as the natural effect; with to or on.

more.text: Following by necessary inference or rational deduction; as a proposition consequent to other propositions.
Effect; that which follows a cause.

example.quote: In it one body has the legislative, executive, and judicial powers; but the want of efficient powers has prevented the dangers naturally consequent on the union of these.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 6, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
